title: Evidence of valence bond solid and quantum paramagnetism in the $J_1$--$J_2$--$J_3$ Heisenberg model from pseudofermion functional renormalization group
authors: Gün Günal, Erhai Zhao, Ahmet Keleş
abstract: Motivated by recent tensor network studies reporting a quantum spin liquid (QSL) within the quantum paramagnetic (QP) regime, we investigate numerically the zero-temperature phase diagram of the $J_1$--$J_2$--$J_3$ Heisenberg model on the square lattice using the pseudofermion functional renormalization group (pf-fRG). Thanks to improved frequency resolution and larger lattice truncations, we are able to explore a significantly larger parameter space than previous pf-fRG work to map out the phase boundary of an extended QP region. We further resolve possible bond order within the QP regime by measuring the dimer response to small deformations in $J_1$, i.e. bond anisotropy that breaks the point-group symmetry of the Hamiltonian. The functional renormalization group flow of the dimer susceptibility suggests that the QP window splits into two: a region where it grows continuously down to the lowest energy scale to signal valence bond solid (VBS) order, and another region where it reaches a peak at a finite scale and is subsequently suppressed to indicate a QSL.
summary: This theoretical study uses the pseudofermion Functional Renormalization Group (pf-fRG) to map the phase diagram of the $J_1$-$J_2$-$J_3$ Heisenberg model. By analyzing the flow of the dimer susceptibility, the authors resolve the Quantum Paramagnetic (QP) regime into two distinct regions: one indicative of Valence Bond Solid (VBS) order and another suggesting a Quantum Spin Liquid (QSL) candidate. This refines our understanding of quantum magnetism in frustrated lattices.
main_problem: The study aims to map the zero-temperature phase diagram of the $J_1$-$J_2$-$J_3$ Heisenberg model to distinguish between Quantum Spin Liquid (QSL) and Valence Bond Solid (VBS) phases within the Quantum Paramagnetic (QP) regime.
main_result: The analysis suggests the QP window splits into two distinct regions: one characterized by continuously growing dimer susceptibility (indicating VBS order), and another showing a peak followed by suppression (suggesting a QSL candidate).
method: The research employs the pseudofermion Functional Renormalization Group (pf-fRG) technique, analyzing the flow of various susceptibilities as a function of the renormalization scale.
model_or_system: The system is the $J_1$-$J_2$-$J_3$ Heisenberg model defined on the square lattice, described by a Hamiltonian involving nearest-neighbor ($J_1$), next-nearest-neighbor ($J_2$), and third-nearest-neighbor ($J_3$) couplings.
key_observables: Dimer susceptibility ($\chi_{\Lambda}^d$), static spin susceptibility ($\chi_{\Lambda}(\Omega=0)$), and the flow behavior of these quantities with the renormalization scale ($\Lambda$).
important_parameters: The ratios $J_2/J_1$ and the inclusion of $J_3$ are critical parameters used to traverse different magnetic regimes (AFM, QP, VBS, stripe).
main_assumptions: The pf-fRG flow is truncated at the six-point level using the Katanin truncation scheme, and the detection of VBS order relies on adding a small source field ($\delta$) to break symmetry.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram across different couplings, showing how the flow of dimer susceptibility ($\chi_{\Lambda}^d$) changes qualitatively across the QP window, distinguishing between continuous growth (VBS) and peaking/suppression (QSL candidate).
paper_structure: The paper systematically investigates the phase diagram by analyzing the flow of susceptibilities using pf-fRG. It first establishes the general phase boundaries and then uses the dimer susceptibility flow to resolve the QP regime into distinct VBS and QSL-like regions.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical probe into the complex interplay between competing magnetic interactions ($J_1, J_2, J_3$) in frustrated quantum magnets, offering a sophisticated tool (pf-fRG) to differentiate between competing exotic ground states like VBS and QSL.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Phase diagram of the J1–J2–J3 model on square lattice obtained with pf-fRG where each dot represents an independent calculation. The colors correspond to the iden- tified phases: antiferromagnetic (AFM) order in green, stripe order in orange, spiral order in brown, and the quantum para- magnetic (QP) regime in blue. We distinguish two different QP phases: candiate qauntum spin liquid (QSL) and valence bond solid (VBS), separated with red dashed area, by moni- toring the dimer susceptibility flows (see main text).

FIG. 2. Static spin susceptibility in the J1–J2 model. Up- per panel: flow of χΛ(q) in the leading momentum channel for representative points in the AFM phase (J2/J1 = 0.35, green), the candidate QSL regime (J2/J1 = 0.55, red), the VBS regime (J2/J1 = 0.60, blue), and the stripe phase (J2/J1 = 0.75, orange). The magnetically ordered phases exhibit an instability that terminates the flow at a critical scale Λc, whereas within the QP window the susceptibility flows smoothly down to the lowest scale Λ = 0.05J1. Lower panel: the corresponding momentum-resolved susceptibility χΛ(q) evaluated at the end of the flow.

FIG. 3. Renormalization flow of the dimer susceptibility χΛ d in the J1–J2 model for selected values of J2. The horizontal gray dotted line marks the unperturbed initial value χd = 1. In the AFM phase (J2/J1 = 0.35, green) the perturbation is sup- pressed before the flow breaks down. In the frustrated regime (J2/J1 = 0.55, red), χΛ d grows initially but is ultimately sup- pressed at low energy scales. In the VBS regime, it instead displays a significant enhancement down to the lowest scales smoothly, (J2/J1 = 0.60 and 0.65, solid and dashed blue, re- spectively). In the stripe phase (J2/J1 = 0.75, orange), the dimer susceptibility plateaus and the magnetic instability ter- minates the flow.

FIG. 4. Static spin susceptibility along the J2 = 0 cut. Up- per panel: flow of χΛ(q) in the leading momentum channel for representative points in the AFM phase (J3/J1 = 0.2), the QP regime (J3/J1 = 0.35 and 0.6), and the spiral phase (J3/J1 = 1.0 and 3.0). The magnetically ordered phases ex- hibit an instability that terminates the flow at a critical scale Λc, whereas within the QP window the susceptibility flows smoothly down to the lowest scale Λ = 0.05J1. Lower panel: the corresponding momentum-resolved susceptibility χΛ(q) for the AFM (J3/J1 = 0.2), the QP (J3/J1 = 0.35), and spiral (J3/J1 = 1.0) states, with the susceptibility profiles evaluated at the end of the flow.

FIG. 5. The flow of the dimer susceptibility χΛ d for selected points. The gray dotted line indicates the unperturbed value χd = 1. The upper panel shows the J2 = 0 cut. The candi- date QSL regime (J3 = 0.35, red) is characterized by a sup- pression of χΛ d towards the end of the flow. In contrast, the VBS phase (J3 = 0.6, blue) exhibits a steady, continuous en- hancement. The AFM (J3 = 0.2, green) and spiral (J3 = 1.0, brown) phases undergo a magnetic flow breakdown at large scale Λ. The lower panel shows the J2 = 0.6 cut.
